firmwareNotes: This CC map is for the WAVE BARD variant only (the stereo sample player). It is the variant in the user's koii-sampler skill, but confirm the unit on the desk. USB MIDI was added in Wave Bard firmware 1.1. The latest firmware is 1.6 (USB descriptor fix: the unit now names itself 'Kastle 2 Wave Bard', with better Linux support). In 1.5 the lowest two MIDI octaves started playing samples at original pitch. Source: manual v1.5 (2025-11-01) and Bastl's MIDI cheat sheet (June 2025). The other Kastle 2 variants also have USB MIDI but DIFFERENT maps: Kastle 2 Alchemist (synth; firmware 1.7 added velocity and sustain) and Kastle 2 FX Wizard (effects; USB MIDI since firmware 1.2). Do not use this chart for them.

sources.title: Kastle 2 Wave Bard user manual v1.5 (USB MIDI IMPLEMENTATION chapter)
Wave Bard firmware release notes v1.6
Wave Bard FAQ ('USB-C is used for powering..., firmware updates/loading samples, and for sending/receiving USB MIDI')

usb.notes: USB-C carries power, firmware updates, sample loading and USB MIDI in and out [docs]. No driver is mentioned and it is used directly with DAWs, so it is assumed class compliant [inferred]. No USB audio is mentioned; audio goes through 3.5 mm jacks [docs/inferred]. The port name comes from the 1.6 USB descriptor fix [inferred], so match /kastle/i. It does not charge batteries over USB [docs].

identity.notes: Nothing documented. Do not rely on SysEx.

channels.receive: One channel for both input and output. It applies to Note, Pitch Bend and CC. Clock has no channel [docs]. Default channel is not stated (probably 1) [unknown].
channels.notes: To set the channel: enter Advanced Settings (hold SHIFT+BANK for 2 s), then hold SHIFT, press BANK N times and release; the light blinks N times. To MIDI-learn instead: in Advanced Settings hold BANK for at least 1 s, send any Note, CC or Pitch Bend from the web app, then release. Leave Advanced Settings with SHIFT+BANK for 2 s or a power cycle [docs]. MIDI-learn is the most reliable step to do on camera.

notes.description: Responds to Note On only. Velocity and Note Off are ignored, and the sample plays its LENGTH envelope [docs].

map.0-47: Select and trigger samples 1-12 of the current bank; each octave starts at C = sample 1 [docs]
map.0-23: Played at original sample pitch (since firmware 1.5) [docs]
map.48-127: Trigger the current sample, pitched: 48 = -2 oct, 72 (C4) = original pitch, 96 = +2 oct [docs]
map.pitchBend: +/-7 semitones, only after a Note On (MIDI Pitch mode) [docs]

parameters.name: FILTER
parameters.notes: Bipolar: middle = open, left = lowpass, right = highpass [docs]. Center value is about 64 [inferred]. Applies immediately.

parameters.name: FX
parameters.notes: Center = no effect. Left = tempo-synced delay (3/8). Right = chorus/flanger/soft-clip [docs].

parameters.name: PITCH
parameters.notes: Top right knob. Moving it via CC returns the unit to Patch Pitch [docs].

parameters.name: SAMPLE
parameters.notes: Applied only right before the next trigger or Note On [docs]

parameters.name: LENGTH
parameters.notes: Center = shortest envelope, right = forward and longer. Applied only on next trigger [docs].

parameters.name: TEMPO
parameters.notes: While MIDI clock is running, TEMPO selects the clock divider [docs]

parameters.name: BANK
parameters.notes: 0-127 is scaled to the number of banks. Applied on next trigger [docs].

parameters.name: Input Gain
parameters.notes: Up to +12 dB [docs]. Avoid in the demo.

parameters.name: Output Volume
parameters.notes: Clamp in the driver. A jump to 127 can blast headphones.

parameters.name: Reset All Controllers
parameters.notes: Gives control back to the physical knobs. Received CC values otherwise hold until a knob is moved [docs].

transport.notes: Syncs to USB MIDI clock automatically, and it takes priority over SYNC IN and the internal clock [docs]. Start resets the pattern generator and waits for clock; Stop stops the sequencer; Continue resumes [docs]. It sends clock and transport only while it is not receiving clock [docs]. Ignore-clock options live in Advanced Settings (LFO knob).

unsafeMessages: CC 7 (Output Volume) at high values: hearing and speaker risk. Clamp it, e.g. to 100 or less.
CC 9 (Input Gain): up to +12 dB, so feedback or clipping is possible when a line input is patched.
CC 121 resets all received CC values to the physical knob positions, which causes sudden jumps in sound.
MIDI clock from the app overrides the Kastle's internal and SYNC tempo. Send it on purpose, or not at all.

demo.visualFeedback: Weak. The knobs are plain potentiometers and do not move. The LEDs show bank colour and LFO state only. Put the CC values on screen in the web UI instead.
demo.audibleFeedback: Immediate for FILTER, FX, PITCH and volume. SAMPLE, LENGTH and BANK changes are heard only on the next trigger or Note On.
risks: Variant mix-up: this map is Wave Bard only.
The default MIDI channel is undocumented, so MIDI-learn it first.
Physical knob moves override the CC values.
Patch cables change what a knob does (modulation inputs). Unpatch everything for a predictable demo.
